about: The rights register (CONTEXT.md; PLAN 6 and 6.1; ADR 0006, ADR 0020): one row per Origin and per intermediary Channel, with the terms read, a proposal, and Alex's decision. This file is the single table. docs/v2/rights-register.md and packages/core/src/rights-register.generated.ts are generated from it (npm run gen); atlas/rights.py reads it. A row permits something on a public Surface only when its decision is signed by Alex. The builder proposes and never fills in a decision.

rows.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics
rows.used_for: CPI, payrolls, unemployment, participation, wages. v2.0 (M7, M13).

capture.note: CPI-U all items (not adjusted and seasonally adjusted), the unemployment rate and total nonfarm payrolls, monthly, for the ten years ending this year: one request without a key.

quotes: everything that we publish, both in hard copy and electronically, is in the public domain, except for previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations
You are free to use our public domain material without specific permission
we do ask that you cite the Bureau of Labor Statistics as the source

terms.note: The site refused the automated request (HTTP 403).

rows.attribution: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

proposal.note: Public domain by the Bureau's own statement. Cite the Bureau on every figure and download.

open_questions: The API terms of service and the API FAQ were not read: bls.gov refused the automated request for both (HTTP 403, 2026-11-11). Read them before signing.

Limits without a key, as far as M7 could check them on 2026-11-11 by asking the API: a request for more than ten years is cut to ten years from its start year, with a message; an unknown series is left out, with a message. The capture job asks for ten years and treats any message as an incomplete answer. The daily limit on requests without a key is believed to be 25 and was not confirmed from the page; the job makes one request per run, two runs a day.

rows.name: Bureau of Economic Analysis

quotes: Citations are appreciated and appropriate.

terms.note: The sign-up form asks for agreement to published terms of service; the terms document itself was not read.

rows.attribution: Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.

proposal.note: U.S. federal works are not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). That is the basis proposed here; the pages read do not themselves state a licence. Cite the Bureau.

open_questions: Read the API terms of service when the key is requested, and record any required notice or request limit here before M15.

rows.name: Census Bureau
rows.used_for: Construction spending (C30 files), retail, housing. v2.0 top lines (M16); v2.1.

quotes: This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau.
You may not modify or falsely represent content accessed through the API and still claim the source is the Census Bureau.
Use the suggested citation if one is provided with the publication, data, code, or tool.

rows.attribution: Source: U.S. Census Bureau.

proposal.note: U.S. federal works are not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). That is the basis proposed here; the pages read do not themselves state a licence. The plan uses published files, not the API. If the API is ever used, the API notice quoted above must be shown.

open_questions: The API terms forbid using the data to identify a person or business. Macro Atlas uses published aggregates only; confirm that is enough.

rows.name: Treasury Fiscal Data
origins: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service
rows.used_for: Debt, Monthly Treasury Statement receipts and outlays. v2.0 (M13).

capture.note: Total public debt outstanding, daily since 1993-04-01, the whole table on each run (one page of about 2.8 MB on 2026-11-11).

quotes: The data is offered free, without restriction, and available to copy, adapt, redistribute, or otherwise use for non-commercial or commercial purposes.
The data on this site is available to copy, adapt, redistribute, or otherwise use for non-commercial and commercial purposes.

rows.attribution: Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Fiscal Data.

proposal.note: Open by the Bureau's own statement, with no condition attached.

rows.name: Federal Reserve Board
origins: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
rows.used_for: H.15 rates, H.10 exchange rates, H.4.1 balance sheet, Z.1 net worth, through the Data Download Program. v2.0 (M13).

Please cite to the Board as the source of the information.

rows.attribution: Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.

proposal.note: Public domain by the Board's own statement, unless a release says otherwise. Cite the Board.

open_questions: Some releases carry data the Board marks as coming from a non-Board source. Each series added in M13 is checked for such a mark before it is listed under this row.

rows.name: Energy Information Administration
rows.used_for: Energy prices; generation and capacity. v2.0 headline (M15); depth in v2.1. Needs a free API key from Alex.

quotes: U.S. government publications are in the public domain and are not subject to copyright protection.

you should use an acknowledgment, which includes the publication date

rows.attribution: Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (with the publication date).

proposal.note: Public domain by the Administration's own statement. The acknowledgement carries the publication date.

open_questions: API rate limits are still unverified (PLAN 6).

rows.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis), as a channel
rows.used_for: Was v1's main channel (83 entries). Not fetched, stored or shown publicly by v2 (PLAN 6, 6.1).

quotes: you are free to use FRED for your own non-commercial, educational, and personal uses
Series with a copyright notice are owned by third parties and have special restrictions.
terms.note: The same page lists, among the things a user may not do: storing, caching or archiving any portion of the content; republishing or distributing it; and using it to develop or train software. Those items are paraphrased here, not quoted.

proposal.note: Do not clear. The terms as read forbid storing and republishing what FRED serves, whatever the status of the underlying series. v2 re-sources every series from its origin instead. Clearing this row would also need a dated amendment to ADR 0006.

open_questions: Whether to ask the Bank for written permission is D2, Alex's decision.
v1's public site and committed data file already hold values fetched through FRED. That exposure is the separate question D4.

rows.name: ALFRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis), as a channel
rows.used_for: Would give provider vintages. Not used by v2.

terms.note: The request did not complete. ALFRED is served by the same Bank; its terms are assumed, not confirmed, to match FRED's.

proposal.note: Do not clear. Treat as FRED until the page is read. Vintages come from v2's own capture (M7, M8) and, later, the origin agencies' archives.

open_questions: Read the page and record whether its terms differ from FRED's.

rows.name: Yahoo Finance, as a channel
rows.used_for: Was v1's channel for index levels, exchange rates and commodities (25 entries). Withheld from every public surface (PLAN 6).

quotes: Unless you have explicit written permission, you must not reproduce, modify, rent, lease, sell, trade, distribute, transmit, broadcast
terms.note: The same terms forbid collecting data from the services by automated means without prior permission (paraphrased).

proposal.note: Do not clear. Exchange rates and interest rates are re-sourced from the Federal Reserve Board. Index levels (S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq and others) have no free publishable source and stay withheld.

open_questions: The index providers (S&P Dow Jones Indices, Nasdaq and others) own the index levels whatever the channel; a publishable source would need their licence.

rows.name: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Real-Time Data Set
rows.used_for: Provider vintages for GDP, payrolls, unemployment, CPI. v2.1, after a spike.

terms.note: No terms-of-use page was found at the addresses tried (HTTP 404). The site footer reads: Copyright 2026. All rights reserved.

proposal.note: No proposal to allow until terms for the data set are found and read. The footer reserves all rights, so nothing is assumed.

open_questions: Find the terms that apply to the Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists, or ask the Bank (PLAN 6: terms unclear).

rows.name: International Monetary Fund
rows.used_for: Japan CPI fix; G20 CPI and exchange rates (SDMX 3.0). v2.0 (M14). Later WEO GDP and commodity prices, v2.2.

quotes: Distributed or reproduced Data must appear accurately with attribution to the IMF as the source.
Users shall not infringe upon the integrity of the Data
terms.note: As summarised from the page: data may be downloaded, copied, published and distributed with attribution; commercial reuse needs permission; automated bulk downloading needs explicit permission; use to train large language models needs explicit permission.

rows.attribution: Source: International Monetary Fund.

proposal.note: Allow display, download and storage with attribution, for a non-commercial site. Do not describe as usable for model training: the terms as summarised reserve that.

open_questions: Does a daily request to the SDMX API for a few dozen series count as automated bulk downloading, which the terms as summarised reserve? Confirm with the page or with the Fund before M14.
The wording was read through a tool that returns short extracts. Open the page before signing (PLAN 6: IMF reuse wording still unverified).

terms.note: The site refused the automated request (HTTP 403).

rows.attribution: Source: OECD.

rows.name: Bank for International Settlements
rows.used_for: Policy rates for 18 G20 economies and the euro area. v2.2.

quotes: The use of the statistics is unrestricted, provided that:
if the statistics are reproduced, the BIS must be cited in your publication or product as the source of the statistics;
No other use is permissible.

rows.attribution: Source: Bank for International Settlements.

The permission granted above does not extend to any material whose copyright is identified as belonging to a third-party

rows.attribution: Source: Eurostat.

open_questions: Some data sets are marked as third-party or non-commercial only; each one added is checked for that mark.

numerical data and data in Simple tables, graphs, and so forth are not subject to copyright

rows.name: Bureau of Transportation Statistics

terms.note: The quotation is the citation the page asks for. The page states no licence.

proposal.note: U.S. federal works are not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). That is the basis proposed here; the pages read do not themselves state a licence. Use the citation the page gives.

rows.name: Our World in Data
rows.used_for: COVID history. v2.2.

Most of the data on Our World in Data comes from third-party providers (such as the WHO, UN, and World Bank) and is subject to the license terms of those providers.

rows.attribution: Source: Our World in Data (CC BY), with the upstream provider named.

open_questions: The COVID series rest on WHO data. Decide whether the series wanted counts as collated by Our World in Data or needs a WHO row.

rows.name: National statistics offices (placeholder)
rows.used_for: G20 unemployment gaps the OECD does not fill (ONS, INDEC, Stats SA, MOSPI, BPS and others). v2.2.

proposal.note: Nothing to allow. A placeholder so that the plan's source is not forgotten.

open_questions: Add one row per office when v2.2 chooses them.
rows.terms_note: No office has been chosen yet, so no terms have been read. This row matches no real origin; each office gets its own row before any of its data is fetched.

rows.name: Gallup (hand-entered presidential approval)
rows.used_for: Presidential approval, quarterly averages, entered by hand in v1. v2.0 hand-entered files (M16).

terms.note: No terms-of-use page was found at the addresses tried (HTTP 404).

proposal.note: No proposal to allow. Gallup is a private company and its figures are its own; nothing is assumed from an unread page. Consider a source with clear terms for approval ratings, or written permission.

open_questions: Read Gallup's terms, or choose another source for approval ratings, before M16.

rows.name: Wikipedia (hand-entered election results)
rows.used_for: Election popular-vote margins, entered by hand in v1 from election infoboxes. v2.0 hand-entered files (M16).

quotes: Reuse of content that we host is welcome, though exceptions exist for content contributed under "fair use" or similar exemptions under applicable copyright law. Any reuse must comply with the underlying license(s).
terms.note: Text on Wikipedia is under CC BY-SA 4.0, which asks that adaptations carry the same licence.

rows.attribution: Source: Wikipedia, with the article and the date read (CC BY-SA 4.0).

proposal.note: Do not clear; re-source instead. Election results are public facts with official records (the Federal Election Commission, the Clerk of the House, the National Archives). M16 should enter them from those, each with its citation, which avoids a share-alike condition on Macro Atlas's downloads.

open_questions: Choose the official source for presidential and congressional results in M16 and give it its own row.

rows.name: Hand-entered facts from the public record
origins: Macro Atlas, from the public record
rows.used_for: Terms of government (who held the presidency and each chamber, and when), each entry with a citation. v2.0 hand-entered files (M16).
rows.attribution: Each entry carries its own citation.

proposal.note: Dates and office-holders are facts of public record, entered by hand with a citation each. A file that takes its figures from a private compiler does not belong under this row.

open_questions: M16 decides which hand-entered files qualify and names the record each one cites.
rows.terms_note: There is no single terms page: each entry cites the official record it was taken from.

rows.name: Macro Atlas, computed series
rows.used_for: Derived series the engine computes (M11). The row covers the computation only: every input is asked about on its own row, and the most restrictive answer wins.
rows.attribution: Computed by Macro Atlas from the sources named.

proposal.note: Allow. This adds nothing to what the inputs allow and cannot widen it.

rows.terms_note: Macro Atlas's own work; there are no outside terms to read.

rows.name: Macro Atlas, synthetic fixture
rows.used_for: The made-up release used by tests, previews and CI (fixtures/public).
rows.attribution: Synthetic data, not a measurement of anything.

proposal.note: Allow, when a milestone needs fixture values on a public Surface in its tests (the release writer, M9). Until it is signed the fixture, like everything else, is refused by the gate on staging and production, and the site's tests of the production Surface expect that; signing this row is done together with changing those tests.

rows.terms_note: Macro Atlas's own synthetic numbers; there are no outside terms to read.
